purpose: Non-admission discovery registry of distinct source-original CAT event reports, impact estimates and product-limited validation resources; no new data admission or source-byte publication.

entries.name: DFO Global Flood Records v0.9.0
entries.provider: Dartmouth Flood Observatory / University of Colorado
entries.spatial_scope: global; large reported flood events, not uniformly complete across countries
entries.temporal_scope: Publisher describes January 1985 to December 2023 for v0.9.0, but the published CSV preview contains January 2024 records; actual coverage boundary requires reconciliation
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Zenodo record 19288171; downloadable Global_Flood_Records.csv and GeoPackage; catalogue lists event date intervals, affected area approximations, causes, fatalities, displaced people and source labels
entries.note: Publisher FloodRecords wiki states CC0 for this event-record product and points to the v0.9.0 Zenodo release; independently inspect its bundled LICENSE.txt and pin exact downloaded bytes before any admission. Legacy Flood Observatory archive and event inundation raster/maps may have different noncommercial terms; CC0 must never be carried over to those separate files. Catalogue area affected is not measured flood-depth raster or insured loss; repeated, fragmented and cross-border events need manual identity review. Observed source inconsistency: v0.9.0 CSV starts with January 2024-dated rows despite its stated December 2023 endpoint; the source release is not yet date-range validated. Original CSV uses M/D/YY dates, not ISO YYYY-MM-DD; any importer must parse them unambiguously and preserve the raw receipt.

entries.name: NOAA Storm Prediction Center Severe Weather GIS through 2025
entries.provider: NOAA National Weather Service Storm Prediction Center
entries.temporal_scope: tornado reports 1950-2025; hail and damaging wind 1955-2025; site updated April 2026
entries.resolution_or_granularity: CSV-derived downloadable event point and path ESRI Shapefiles; report attributes and coordinates, with a provider changelog of historical corrections and changing identifiers
entries.note: SPC states the GIS derives from official Storm Data CSV, so it is not independent of NOAA NCEI Storm Events. For tornadoes missing end points, the provider makes artificial short LineStrings using 0.0001 degree offsets: do not read them as physical swaths. The 24 April 2026 changelog also changes newer om_number identifiers. Version and SHA-pin releases, preserve original report IDs, report types, dates and source bias. Reports are not insured claims or complete event footprints.

entries.name: USGS ComCat Did You Feel It event products
entries.provider: United States Geological Survey Earthquake Hazards Program
entries.spatial_scope: United States and selected global earthquakes with voluntary responses
entries.temporal_scope: event-dependent historical and ongoing responses; no continuous complete global coverage asserted
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Per-event versioned ComCat dyfi products including city or ZIP aggregates, geocoded 1 km and 10 km GeoJSON intensity files, response counts and product update timestamps
entries.note: DYFI combines volunteered macroseismic experiences into aggregated intensity, not instrument-measured PGA, building damage, insurance claims or unbiased exposure sampling. Freeze ComCat event ID plus source/type/code/update-time to avoid silently comparing revised preferred versions. A missing response must never become zero shaking; exclude individual raw responses absent explicit release and privacy review.

entries.name: USGS ComCat PAGER earthquake impact estimates
entries.provider: United States Geological Survey Earthquake Hazards Program
entries.spatial_scope: significant earthquakes worldwide for which a losspager product exists
entries.temporal_scope: event-dependent historical and current ComCat products; coverage and updates vary by event
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Versioned losspager event product; pager.xml plus json/losses.json, json/exposures.json, alerts, population exposure and alert-level summaries
entries.note: PAGER fatalities and economic losses are MODELLED estimates informed by ShakeMap, LandScan exposure and regional historical-impact relationships, not observed losses or insured claims. Never train against PAGER and then declare independent loss validation against it, and do not infer treaty losses. Pin product version and all upstream assumptions; protect against changes to preferred ComCat products.

entries.name: Copernicus Emergency Management Service Rapid Mapping
entries.provider: European Commission Joint Research Centre / Copernicus CEMS
entries.spatial_scope: global emergency activations; coverage limited to specific requested areas of interest
entries.temporal_scope: activation-triggered archive and near-event response; no global regular event-frequency series
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Activation and product level geospatial delineation, grading and reference maps; selected vector Shapefiles, KMZ, georeferenced TIFF and map products
entries.note: JRC says data are open access with exceptions: this statement is NOT a blanket redistribution approval for each activation/product. Preserve activation ID, mapping area, production time, satellite date, mapping type, licence and byte receipts. Delineation or damage grading from emergency mapping is a constrained observation, not a sampled catalogue of all events, exact flood depths or insurer losses; avoid extrapolating unmapped areas as zero.

entries.name: UNDRR DesInventar Sendai national disaster loss databases
entries.provider: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction and contributing national institutions
entries.spatial_scope: many country and regional databases, with highly variable geographic and historical coverage
entries.temporal_scope: country-specific historical intervals and periodic updates; not one uniform global time series
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Country-hosted event and subnational disaster impact records with possible CSV or Excel exports, hazard categories, human impacts, affected housing and reported economic indicators
entries.note: The Apache-style licence described by the publisher applies to DesInventar SOFTWARE, not automatically to separately contributed national DATABASES. Dataset rights, provenance and export availability must be checked by country. Differences in event definitions, reporting thresholds, spatial units, nominal-currency values and completeness prohibit automatic pooling or translation into insured CAT loss.

entries.name: USGS Global Flood Impacts Database (GFID): original contributed flood datasets
entries.provider: US Geological Survey and underlying DFO / EM-DAT / HANZE / DesInventar providers
entries.spatial_scope: global provider inputs with separate country/time coverage; original upstream coverage is heterogeneous
entries.temporal_scope: USGS GFID catalog updated 2026-10-05; individual included original dataset versions and time ranges require exact archive verification
entries.resolution_or_granularity: USGS data release DOI 10.5066/P135ARGI; separate DFO_FloodData.csv, EMDAT_FloodData.xlsx, HANZE_Events_v3.csv and DesInventar country records/aggregate; source-native IDs, geography and report fields
entries.note: This is a collection of copied original upstream records, not a new independent flood-observation source. USGS public access does not grant uniform redistribution or commercial-use rights to contributed EM-DAT, HANZE, DesInventar or DFO inputs. The DFO_FloodData.csv and HANZE_Events_v3.csv schemas described in the release are not automatically identical to our separately pinned DFO v0.9.0 and HANZE v3.0.2-beta CSVs. Freeze individual file versions, hashes, source fields, attribution and third-party conditions; do not reuse release aggregate counts as unique physical disasters.

entries.name: USGS Global Flood Impacts Database (GFID): aggregated geocoded event and duplicate-screening products
entries.provider: US Geological Survey and underlying DFO / EM-DAT / HANZE / DesInventar providers
entries.spatial_scope: 197 countries and territories represented by selected provider inputs; not exhaustive world flood observations
entries.temporal_scope: USGS release metadata catalog updated 2026-10-05; upstream temporal windows and aggregation snapshot require exact original publication proof
entries.resolution_or_granularity: 136,642 reported flood event records, 82,245 with at least one reported nonzero impact; AggregatedFloodData.xlsx, geocoded DFO/EM-DAT/HANZE/DesInventar records and Potential_Duplicate_Events.csv using 30-day and 25-km screening; representative EPSG:4326 point coordinates
entries.note: The 30-day and 25-km proximity file contains only possible duplicate/overlapping records, NOT confirmed same-event identity. It must not be treated as independent validation of DFO, HANZE, EM-DAT or DesInventar. USGS GEO_LAT/GEO_LON and HANZE LAT/LON are representative coordinates for indexing (often region-derived), not flood footprints, exact impact addresses or flood depths. Economic-loss columns use different currencies, baselines and definitions; reported nonzero impacts are not insured claims. Compare only version-matched source IDs and verified input SHA256, retaining exact source-specific metadata and licence gates.
